newsitem.title: Australia: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 5.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian rugby union winger David Campese said yesterday that his Australian representative career is probably over, as a knee injury has forced him out of the NSW team for the two-match interstate series with Queensland, which were to be his last games at the provincial level. Campese is considering lucrative, multi-season offers to play club football in England or Italy. Page 20.

Australian Football side North Melbourne's football manager Geoff Walsh said captain Wayne Carey was rated a 60-40 chance to play in the Monday night game against Fremantle. Carey has missed the first half of the season due to a shoulder injury suffered n the first round of this year's competition. Page 20.

The Sydney United and South Melbourne soccer teams are expected to receive details today of charges laid against them by Soccer Australia for bringing the game into disrepute after a crowd invasion at a preliminary final two weeks ago. It has been revealed that United supporters also attacked a SBS television crew, the network being a long-time supporter of soccer in Australia. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Olympic swimmer Scott Miller yesterday denied that he had been expelled from the Australian Institute of Sport due to an altercation at a nightclub. Miller says Australia's head coach Don Talbot told him he had too many outside commitments to warrant having an AIS scholarship. Miller said sponsorship commitments meant he had to miss training sessions. Page 50.

The Canterbury Bulldogs Super League team has stepped up their school education program following reports that schoolboys boasted they had "bashed the coppers" during a crowd disturbance at Monday night's game against Penrith. The club has also installed video surveillance cameras at their home ground and police have promised to increase patrol numbers and introduce dogs squads at matches in an effort to curb crowd violence at games. The club has denied that the violence is a race issue. Page 49.

Australian soccer player Damian Mori was sent off during the last game of the Super Stars series at Parramatta Stadium last night for a second bookable offence late in the first half. National coach Terry Venables, who will name his 22-man squad for the World Cup either today or tomorrow, was exasperated at the decision to send Mori off even though the referee was technically correct. Page 49.
THE AGE

The Channel 7 television network has said it might have to review its arrangement with pay-TV broadcaster Optus Vision next year so that it was assured of showing the Australian Football League match of the day on its replay show. The deal struck at the sart of this season gives Optus Vision first choice of the replays of 18 games during the season. Page B8.

Victorian Racing Club stewards yesterday announced a restructuring of the track ratings procedure, following criticism that present track readings were inaccurate. Last week in three Victorian country meetings had to downgrade their track conditions during the day. VRC chief steward Des Gleeson said the new guidelines involved closer liaison between race club officials and stewards in the lead up to race meetings and would restore confidence in the racing industry. Page B6.

The Australian Football League said yesterday that club side Hawthorn's plan to roof the seating areas at Waverley Park was premature and possibly irrelevant. Hawthorn's plan required funding from a A$5 surcharge on all patrons attending the ground. The FL will call for tenders for Waverley Park in August after construction of the Docklands project begins. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Tasmanian cricketer Jamie Cox will be offered the vice-captaincy of the Victorian cricket side in an attempt to lure him to the Victorian team. This would effectively make him captain due to leading player Shane Warne's national team commitments. Cox promted the offer last month when he said the chance of captaining Victoria would outweigh any final inducement. Page 78.

Touring car driver Wayne Gardner has pulled out of the Shell Supercar Series with four rounds remaining, due to the high cost of V8 Supercar racing. The former world motorcycle champion will contest the final round at Sydney's Oran Park and the long-distace races at Sandown and Bathurst, but the future of the team after those three races is uncertain. Page 79.

The Australian cricket side last night named batsman Greg Blewett and bowler Jason Gillespie, who were both carrying injuries this week, in the team for tonight's first Test at Edgbaston. Blewett still has to pass a last-minute fitness test for a knee injury but is expected to play, and Gillespie has quickly recovered from a bruised toe and trained strongly. Batsman Justin Langer is likely to be 12th man. Page 88.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

A rematch between boxers Kostya Tszyu and Vincent Phillips will be held outdoors in Sydney in November or December this year. Phillips defeated the previously unbeaten Tszyu for the IBF junior welterweight boxing crown with a 10th-round knockout in Atlantc City last Sunday. Page 86.

The top-seeded Australian tennis doubles team of Todd Woodbridge and Mark Woodforde defeated Americans Rick Leach and Jonathon Stark 6-2 7-6 (7-5) yesterday to reach the semi-finals of the French Open, the only Grand Slam tournament they have not yet won.Page 34.

Australian boxer Joe Bugner successfully defended his Pan-Asian Boxing Association heavyweight title on the Gold Coast yesterday when he knocked out Fijian champion Waisiki Ligaloa with a right to the jaw in the seventh round. Page 34.
